doctrine: Segments are built from live activity and verified payroll-style income, never from static account profiles. Recency window: activity within the current live window; income verified by a pay event within the current pay cycle.

markets.note: Highest share of verified mid/high income with current pay events; $10.00 cost per order in the pilot.
Income is not the problem here; pilot cost per order is $20.00 — a timing/placement problem, not a money problem.
Youngest audience and the highest parent-account share — resolve the payer before reading spending power. Evidence still collecting in the pilot; keep capped.

segments_of_note.rule: Viewer aged 18-24 on a parent's account resolves to the parent's verified payroll income for spending power.
segments_of_note.why: Kids stream on their parents' accounts and ask their parents for what they want. The viewer is the demand; the parent is the wallet.

segments_of_note.rule: Households 65+ receiving SNAP benefits, activity-current, low mobility.
segments_of_note.why: SNAP benefits can be used to order food online. Going outside is hard for this segment; the food moment has to be served to them at home. Democratize what nobody else is doing.

source_model: ADP-style payroll + activity feed (simulated sample data)
